Travel page · implementation report

2026-11-15 · branch codex/travel-2027 · base 1230e24

Latest update: map is the focus

The requested dropdown is removed. The map now fills the content width; the unchanged disclaimer follows it at 12px without separate dark panels. Hover, tap, focus or activate a state to show its cap on a parchment label beside it. Tapping outside dismisses the label. Reimbursement values and eligibility are unchanged.

Final production browser run: 14 passed (3.8s). Build, TypeScript and lint exited 0. Existing lint warnings elsewhere remain. Computer Use inspected desktop and 390px phone layouts. The older evidence below records the initial implementation; this section supersedes its selector and sidebar descriptions.

Changed files in this follow-up

  • app/travel/reimbursement/Reimbursement.tsx: Positions the live cap label from state bounds; supports outside dismissal; removes dropdown and its unused state references.
  • app/travel/reimbursement/Reimbursement.module.scss: Adds parchment label styling, removes dropdown styles, tightens legend spacing.
  • app/travel/page.tsx: Keeps disclaimer text inline after its label.
  • app/travel/styles.module.scss: Expands the map to a single full-width column and reduces policy text to 12px without panels.
  • tests/travel/travel.spec.ts: Uses direct keyboard state controls and checks label placement/dismissal, absent dropdown and small policy below map.
  • planning/travel-2027-plan.html: Records approved follow-up scope and completion.
  • saved-results/travel-implementation.md: Updates outcomes and reproduction evidence.
  • saved-results/travel-checks/checks.log: Preserves follow-up red/green, lint, type and build logs.
  • saved-results/travel-label-captures/desktop.webp: Current desktop map and disclaimer screenshot.
  • saved-results/travel-label-captures/mobile.webp: Current phone map and disclaimer screenshot.
  • saved-results/travel-2027-review.html: Updates this complete handoff with current evidence and exact changes.

Checks and limits

  • New map label checks first failed twice on old production layout, then passed on desktop/mobile.
  • New no-dropdown checks first failed twice because the combobox existed; final npm run test:travel -- --workers=2: 14 passed (3.8s).
  • npm run build: exit 0 after final spacing change. npx tsc --noEmit: exit 0. npm run lint: exit 0 before the final spacing-only edit; changed files are formatted again before commit.
  • Searched Choose a state|stateSelect|stateElements|styles.selection in app/travel and tests/travel: no leftover uses. Policy styles are scoped to this page.
  • No separate unit tests: browser tests exercise the actual interactions and layout. No added logging: local display state has no service calls or caught errors.
  • Real Safari/iOS and screen-reader software remain untested. Small states are harder to tap without the dropdown; keyboard focus still exposes every state's rate. No API, schema or policy changes.

Manual check: open localhost:3017/travel; hover/tap Illinois, then another state, then outside the map. Tab through states and press Enter/Escape. Confirm no dropdown, small disclaimer below the map, and working international ticket.

Result and attention needed

The Figma desktop and phone designs now render at /travel with real text, an interactive state map, an international-rate ticket and parchment state labels. No decorative animation. All 14 production browser tests, lint, TypeScript and production build passed.

All 51 state/district amounts are unchanged. Caveat substitutes for Figma Hand; SVG export texture and tree blur differ from Figma’s PNG. These are the main visual limitations. CI/Cloudflare preview are not yet verified. No merge or manual deployment.

Pull request: #564 — Implement 2027 travel reimbursement page. Open; remote CI status not checked in this follow-up. Separate Prizes PR: #563.

Request and visible behavior

Implement the Figma Travel Reimbursement page, match desktop and mobile, make map/ticket work by mouse, touch and keyboard, flag policy differences, and open a PR. Eligibility/opt-in and all six international rates retain existing meaning and amounts. The design matches the visible eligibility text and $100–$400 tier legend; it does not expose per-state or international data, so repository values are preserved, not independently confirmed 2027 policy.

The map and select menu share the existing rates. DC’s existing $250 entry now matches the atlas’s “District of Columbia” name. A live status gives the selected location/rate. The ticket opens on hover or click/tap/Enter and closes via its button, leaving focus, or Escape. The state selector is an addition to support small map targets and keyboard use. Current shared navigation replaces the Figma logo placeholder.

Initial layout evidence (before map follow-up)

Production screenshots at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels: zero page errors; document widths exactly match each viewport. Computer Use separately inspected desktop/mobile, opened international rates, selected Illinois ($100), and confirmed the final 320px ticket.

Accessible state controls

            className={styles.reimbursement}
            aria-label="Reimbursement caps"
        >
            <p className={styles.hint}>
                Hover, tap, or select a state for reimbursement rates
            </p>
            <div className={styles.mapPaper}>
                <ComposableMap
                    projection="geoAlbersUsa"
                    width={800}
                    height={520}
                    projectionConfig={{ scale: 1000 }}
                    className={styles.map}
                    aria-label="United States reimbursement map"
                >
                    <Geographies geography="/us-atlas.json">
                        {({ geographies }) =>
                            geographies
                                .filter(
                                    geo =>
                                        geo.properties.name in
                                        STATE_REIMBURSEMENT
                                )
                                .map(geo => {
                                    const name = geo.properties.name;
                                    const amount = STATE_REIMBURSEMENT[name];
                                    return (
                                        <Geography
                                            key={geo.rsmKey}
                                            geography={geo}
                                            role="button"
                                            tabIndex={0}
                                            aria-label={`${name}: $${amount} reimbursement cap`}
                                            aria-pressed={selected === name}
                                            onMouseEnter={() =>
                                                setHovered(name)
                                            }
                                            onMouseLeave={() => setHovered("")}
                                            onFocus={() => setHovered(name)}
                                            onBlur={() => setHovered("")}
                                            onClick={() => setSelected(name)}
                                            onKeyDown={event => {
                                                if (
                                                    event.key === "Enter" ||
                                                    event.key === " "
                                                ) {
                                                    event.preventDefault();
                                                    setSelected(name);
                                                }
                                            }}
                                            className={styles.state}
                                            data-active={active === name}
                                        />
                                    );
                                })

Full source: app/travel/reimbursement/Reimbursement.tsx. Static artwork has no eligibility text baked into it; HTML supplies the content. The decorative board logo remains artwork.

npx tsc --noEmit Exit 0, no output.

Original/new rate-table comparison PASS: all 51 state/district amounts identical after normalizing the DC name.

An initial test launch could not find a downloaded Chromium executable; using the installed Chrome fixed setup. A later build overlapped with a dev-server check and caused shared .next cache errors; that run was discarded, the dev server stopped, and final checks used a completed production build. Exact logs are saved in saved-results/travel-checks/checks.log.

Limits, skipped checks and assumptions

  • No Safari, real iPhone or screen-reader software run. Chrome touch/keyboard cases plus Computer Use cover the requested interactions.
  • No separate unit tests for static markup: full rendered-flow tests exercise integration and responsive behavior.
  • No new diagnostic logger: selection/disclosure are local display state, with no backend request, persistence, credentials or caught errors. Page errors were captured during screenshot checks: none.
  • Existing dependency audit reported 56 vulnerabilities; broad dependency upgrades are outside this page change.
  • No backend/data-schema changes, PDFs removed, paid calls, or manual deployment.
  • Separate Prizes PR touches the shared route list and package scripts/lockfile too; merging both may require combining these small shared-file changes.

Sibling checks

Searched STATE_REIMBURSEMENT|InteractiveMap|MapLegend|EllipseHeader across the repository. Only Travel used them; superseded components/styles were removed. Compared atlas names to rate keys; DC was the mismatch. Existing shared navigation was reused. Existing public PDFs and previous public assets remain untouched.

Try it

  1. In the worktree run npm ci, npm run build, then npm run start -- --port 3017.
  2. Open http://localhost:3017/travel. Check desktop and a 320–390px phone viewport.
  3. Hover/tap Illinois or select it: $100. Select District of Columbia: $250. Tab to a map state, press Enter or Space.
  4. Open the international ticket by hover/tap/Enter. Check Waterloo $350, Singapore/China/India/UK $500, Not listed $350. Escape closes it and returns focus to the ticket.
  5. In another terminal run npm run test:travel. Tests require installed Google Chrome. Set TRAVEL_BASE_URL for another running server.
